title: test(e2e): fail fast against the local emulator to speed up the suite
body:
## What

When `TEST_API_ROOT` points the e2e suite at a local `telegram-bot-api` (the [telegram-server-emulator](https://github.com/yagop/telegram-server-emulator) pipeline), lower the client `timeoutMs` (30s → 6s) and `maxRetries` (2 → 1) **in emulator mode only**. Live runs against `api.telegram.org` keep the 30s / 2 defaults.

## Why

A handful of group-heavy tests exhaust the bundled bot-api's embedded TDLib per-chat send anti-flood (~20 msgs/min to a megagroup). bot-api then parks the query in a long flood-wait that the emulator can't shorten. With the live defaults, each of those stalled ~90s (30s timeout × 3 attempts) and dominated the whole run.

Failing those flood-blocked calls fast turns a full emulator run from **~21 min → ~7 min**, with the same pass set. The remaining floor is bot-api's own flood control, not the client.

## Notes

- Behaviour is gated on `EMULATOR = Boolean(API_ROOT)`, so nothing changes for real-Telegram CI runs.
- No source/API changes — only the e2e harness client config and its comment.

title: examples: show typed sessions with a spaceship launch flow
body:
### Description

Replace the conversation example's manual Map and type casts with a typed session: name a spaceship, choose a destination, and launch. Each state requires the data collected in earlier steps.

Add mission messages with emojis, session deletion through `/cancel`, and `setMyCommands` for the `/start` and `/cancel` menu. Update the README links and example listing.

title: docs: use bot-specific storage names in session examples
body:
### Description

The session examples use generic storage names, which can cause different bots in the same chat to share session data. Use bot-specific directory names, Redis prefixes, SQL tables, and SQLite files, and explain when separate names are needed.

Validation: `bun run typecheck:examples` and `git diff --check` passed. Full checks and build were not run for this documentation and example configuration change.
